claims.statement: Every spatial representation in the repository uses the [longitude, latitude] order with no conversion layer: CoordinatePair is a two-number tuple used by GeoPoint/GeoLineString, MapLibre's click and drag handlers push event.lngLat.lng then .lat straight into store actions, the Mapbox Directions proxy serializes and re-parses waypoints as a `lng,lat;…` string, and the export document declares coordinate_order "lng_lat" (ADR-0013 supersedes ADR-0007's never-shipped Leaflet exception).

CoordinatePair is an unlabelled tuple, so nothing in the type system distinguishes longitude from latitude; the only automated check that could catch a swapped pair is validatePair's per-number range guard in apps/server/src/domain/geometry.ts, which is unit-tested but imported by no route, so the request path enforces only the shape (a tuple of two finite numbers, LineString ≥ 2 points) and the ::geometry(subtype,4326) write cast is a subtype/SRID assertion rather than a bounds check.

Geometry crosses the persistence boundary only through SQL-expression helpers in apps/server/src/db/queries.ts — reads select ST_AsGeoJSON(col)::jsonb and writes pass ST_GeomFromGeoJSON($json)::geometry(Point,4326)/(LineString,4326) — and because GeoJSON x/y and PostGIS x/y are both lng/lat the round trip is order-preserving while the cast asserts subtype and SRID; the untyped geomFromGeoJSON variant is exported but unused.

The ::geography cast required for meter-based PostGIS math appears in exactly two helpers, pointOnLineMeters (ST_DWithin) and pointDistanceToLineMeters (ST_Distance), both casting both operands, and neither is called by any handler: all executing distance logic (on-line checks, loop endpoints, plotted-path endpoints) is JavaScript haversine, so the rule currently has no live SQL call site; stops.location's GiST index is the only spatial index.

The 100 m endpoint rule (ENDPOINT_TOLERANCE_METERS) is enforced by pathEndpointsOnStops, which validatePlottedPayload turns into a 422 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the failed side and the distance; the end may instead match the first stop for a loop, and the same constant decides in buildDerivedReturn whether the derived return's stop list is rotated (closed loop) or simply reversed.

The 100 m endpoint gate is conditional on the request carrying a stops array: POST /api/routes/:routeId/directions without stops and PUT /api/directions/:directionId that patches only base_polyline write any shape-valid LineString without ever running pathEndpointsOnStops, and because validatePlottedPayload runs before persistPlottedPair the rejected case never opens a transaction.

The 150 m loop-closure tolerance is admin-only (LOOP_CLOSE_TOLERANCE_METERS): it drives polylineClosesOn, the connection helper that appends the last→first closing edge, the plotting store's closingIntent/trustedClosed decisions that re-append the start coordinate before a snap, and resolveConnectingLine's coverage test that decides whether a transient stub is drawn.

pathCoversStops (default 150 m) is a client-only interior-coverage gate requiring every stop to lie within tolerance of some path vertex; the server checks only stop count and endpoints, so a draft whose committed path no longer matches its stops is refused by the admin while the API would accept it, and the admin pairs it with a pathStopIds equality check for stale stop order.

inferDetourFlanks carries its own LOOP_CLOSURE_TOLERANCE_METERS = 150 to decide a base polyline is a loop and to wrap chain-neighbour flanking across the closing arc, and the plotting store treats a newly placed stop within LOOP_CLOSE_TOLERANCE_METERS of the chain's first stop as intent to close the route.

The 30 m detour tolerance (DETOUR_ON_LINE_TOLERANCE_METERS) backs three server checks — entry/exit within 30 m of the base polyline as an exact point-to-segment distance, loop first/last coordinate within 30 m of entry/exit, and rejection of an entry/exit pair 30 m or closer as degenerate — and a PUT touching any of entry, exit or detour_polyline re-runs the loop check against the current stored values so a partial edit cannot drift the loop off its endpoints.

The admin mirrors the 30 m detour gate so authored geometry always passes the server's FR-023 check: DEFAULT_DETOUR_SNAP_TOLERANCE_METERS = 30 is projectPointOnPolyline's default, NODE_TOO_CLOSE_METERS = 30 refuses a degenerate split/merge pair in the detour store, and inferDetourFlanks defaults its snap tolerance to 30 m.

The 20 m overlap tolerance means "the same physical road point" in two display paths: findOppositeOverlapRuns matches vertices within OVERLAP_TOLERANCE_METERS whose travel tangents are opposed (dot < -0.5), requiring ≥ 2 matched vertices for a run and, within one polyline, vertices at least 100 m apart along the line; divergingSegments uses the same 20 m default to keep only the runs where the derived return actually leaves the base corridor.

Overlap offsetting is display-only: shiftOverlapRuns moves each overlapping pass right of its own travel by OVERLAP_OFFSET_METERS = 1 m with a 0 → full → 0 taper over OVERLAP_TAPER_METERS = 30 m, so the two passes end up 2 m apart — the module docstring's "3 m → 6 m total separation" figure is stale relative to the constant that the code and tests use.

Great-circle distance is implemented three times with the same 6 371 000 m radius — coordsDistanceMeters (admin), coordinatesDistanceMeters (server derive), and a private haversineMeters (server validation) — plus a local flat-earth plane in overlap.ts (111 320 m per degree of latitude, longitude scaled by cos(mean latitude)); @komyuter/shared exports no distance helper, and the duplication exists because the admin must pre-validate drafts without a round trip while the server cannot import app code, which leaves the 100 m and 30 m thresholds duplicated as separate constants that must be changed together.

Tolerance comparisons are inclusive in the permissive direction — a distance equal to the tolerance passes (pathEndsOnStops rejects only on >, assertPointOnLine only on >, pathCoversStops and the overlap/separation tests on <=) — while the detour degeneracy clause inverts this by rejecting an entry-exit distance of 30 m or less; the boundary behaviour is pinned by validation.test.ts.

Tolerance gates run at three distinct moments: client authoring gates in the workspace save handler (pathEndsOnStops, pathCoversStops, pathStopIds) and the detour store, server save-time gates that reject with 422 before any write, and render-time display math (overlap offsetting, divergence trimming, transient stub lines) that is never persisted.

The straight-line snapping fallback is treated differently by the two authoring flows: the base-route auto-commit path commits only when the proxy reports snapped: true and otherwise shows a warning, while the detour loop builder persists whatever snapPreview resolves with, so a snapped: false fallback (missing token or upstream error) becomes detour_polyline with mapboxWarning left null because that flag is only set when the snap request itself throws.

Projection and request caps are separate from the tolerance gates: the Mapbox proxy chunks paths at MAPBOX_CHUNK_SIZE = 25 coordinates and drops the duplicated joint coordinate when joining, detour split/merge clicks (and node drags) are projected with a 5000 m corridor so nodes always land back on the base polyline, waypoint clicks are stored at the raw clicked coordinate, and the MAX_DETOUR_VIA_DISTANCE_METERS symbol referenced in the inferDetourFlanks docstring does not exist anywhere in the repository.

reverseCoordinates reverses the coordinate array without swapping ordinates within any pair, so the auto-derived return keeps every [lng, lat] intact and direction of travel is encoded purely in vertex order — the property the direction-aware overlap detector relies on and the reason the two-direction model needs no re-projection (ADR-0008/ADR-0011).
